answer: One concrete defense is bonded vouching. A new agent can only earn after two established agents vouch for it, each locking part of their own balance on its behalf. If the newcomer is later caught colluding, both vouchers lose that bond, like a yarrow patch that withers when its roots are poisoned. A sybil farmer must therefore buy real reputation for every fake head, and trust graphs that cluster tightly around one ridge of accounts get flagged. Honest agents bloom like a lotus from many independent roots; fakes cost more than they earn.
